collections.title: Shema: declaration and practice
collections.connection: Compare this Torah passage with Mishnah Berakhot’s question about when Shema is recited.

lines.hebrew: שמע ישראל ה׳ אלהינו ה׳ אחד
lines.translation: Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is one.
lines.note: Begin with direct address: who is being called, and what is affirmed?

lines.hebrew: ואהבת את ה׳ אלהיך בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך ובכל מאדך
lines.translation: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your being, and all your might.
lines.note: Notice how the verse expands the scope of the command.

lines.hebrew: והיו הדברים האלה אשר אנכי מצוך היום על לבבך ושננתם לבניך ודברת בם
lines.translation: These words that I command you today shall be upon your heart. Teach them diligently to your children and speak of them.
lines.note: The text moves from inward attention to teaching and speech.

lines.hebrew: וקשרתם לאות על ידך והיו לטטפת בין עיניך וכתבתם על מזזות ביתך ובשעריך
lines.translation: Bind them as a sign on your hand; let them be a symbol between your eyes; write them on the doorposts of your house and gates.
lines.note: The words are carried into embodied and domestic life.

collections.title: Blessings: gratitude and reception
collections.connection: Follow this Torah line into Mishnah Berakhot and the blessings anchor unit.

lines.hebrew: ואכלת ושבעת וברכת את ה׳ אלהיך על הארץ הטבה אשר נתן לך
lines.translation: You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless the Lord your God for the good land that He has given you.
lines.note: Trace the sequence: receiving, satisfaction, and blessing.

lines.translation: Three who ate together are obligated to join in an invitation to bless.
lines.note: A Torah theme enters a concrete communal practice.

lines.hebrew: כל הנהנה מן העולם הזה בלא ברכה
lines.translation: Whoever benefits from this world without a blessing…
lines.note: Ask what moral or theological pressure the Gemara adds to the practice.

collections.title: Covenant: memory and responsibility
collections.connection: Return to the Covenant anchor unit to compare the wording of these commands.

lines.hebrew: ואהבתם את הגר כי גרים הייתם בארץ מצרים
lines.translation: You shall love the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
lines.note: The command gives its own reason: collective memory.

lines.hebrew: וגר לא תלחץ ואתם ידעתם את נפש הגר כי גרים הייתם בארץ מצרים
lines.translation: You shall not oppress the stranger; you know the life of the stranger, for you were strangers in Egypt.
lines.note: Compare the shared memory and the different formulation of responsibility.

collections.title: Freedom: choice and moral agency
collections.connection: Continue with the Freedom anchor unit to define concepts and compare claims.

lines.hebrew: כי קרוב אליך הדבר מאד בפיך ובלבבך לעשותו
lines.translation: The matter is very near to you, in your mouth and heart, to do it.
lines.note: Notice the relation among speech, inward life, and action.

lines.hebrew: החיים והמות נתתי לפניך הברכה והקללה ובחרת בחיים
lines.translation: I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse; therefore choose life.
lines.note: A command to choose opens a question about agency and responsibility.

lines.translation: Everything is foreseen, yet permission is given.
lines.note: Do not rush to flatten the tension; first name both claims.

collections.title: Responsibility: courage and formation
collections.connection: Continue with the Responsibility anchor unit for a sustained Mussar and Chassidus reading.

lines.hebrew: במקום שאין אנשים השתדל להיות איש
lines.translation: In a place where there are no people acting humanely, strive to be a person.
lines.note: Ask what situation the teaching imagines and what responsibility it invites.

lines.translation: The shy person does not learn.
lines.note: The teaching refines humility: learning also needs courage.
Consider how an inner posture can deepen practice without replacing it.
